`python3 budget.py 2026-09` now counts only that month's transactions, and with no argument the envelope figures are the same as before.

I ran it against your current file:

| Envelope | No month | 2026-09 | 2026-08 |
|---|---|---|---|
| groceries | 174.60 | 371.55 | 403.05 |
| fuel | 22.85 | 124.75 | 78.10 |
| eating out | 45.75 | 84.25 | 111.50 |
| household | 54.61 | 101.60 | 73.01 |

Two things you didn't ask for:

- **Count line on stderr:** every run now prints a line such as `2026-09: counted 6 of 12 transactions` (or `all time: counted 12 of 12 transactions`). A month with no transactions shows full allocations, so the count is how you tell that apart from a mistyped month. Stdout is unchanged, so anything piping the output is unaffected.
- **Bad arguments:** something that isn't a month (`2026-13`, `sept`) prints a usage message and exits with code 2 instead of reporting on nothing. More than one argument is meant to do the same, but I didn't exercise that case.
